transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-03-15 16:00 UTC
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Ramirez (Redwood SE), Priya Malhotra (CTO, Nova), Ben Carter (Lead ML Eng), Samira Khan (DevOps), Ethan Lee (Product)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on integration patterns for Redwood hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Key topics: SDKs and LangChain/LlamaIndex support, gateway/proxy and on-prem edge cases, rate limits and quotas, and observability hooks (tracing, token-level cost breakdowns). Nova wants predictable latency for inference-heavy features and compliance (data residency + KMS).

Topics:
- Current stack and ML infra
- Integration points (SDKs, HTTP gateway, proxies)
- LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors and examples
- Rate limits, quotas, and burst handling
- Observability: traces, per-route dashboards, token cost attribution
- Security: VPC, KMS, audit logs

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Avery from Redwood, and i have Luis from our SE team, we wanted to start by understanding what you're trying to build with Nova.
[00:12] Priya Malhotra: thanks, Avery, hi all. so we run Nova Insights — we do analytics + recommendations across retailer catalog data, and we're looking to add a retrieval-augmented generation assistant in our product. primary goals are sub-200ms 1-shot latency for small prompts, and consistent cost control.
[00:29] Ben Carter: yeah and mostly offline embeddings + a few online generation endpoints, but the gen path is what worries us — we have spikes during promo events so burstiness is a real thing.
[00:40] Luis Ramirez: got it. quick clarifying q — is the latency requirement end-to-end from your app to model, or just model p99? also are you considering on-prem/private for compliance?
[00:49] Priya: both actually. end-to-end target is 250ms for short completions, and we may need Private (VPC) for certain enterprise customers in eu region. KMS for key management is a must.
[01:02] Avery: cool. to set expectations, Redwood hosted can hit low latency for common open models, Dedicated gives predictable throughput with reserved GPU pools, and Private is our VPC/on-prem option for strict controls. Luis, can you talk about integration surface?
[01:15] Luis: sure. we offer REST + SDKs (python/js/go), and we have first-class adapters for LangChain and LlamaIndex — those are maintained in our examples repo. for high-throughput services you can run behind our gateway or deploy a local proxy that forwards requests to Redwood, we also support stable whitelisted IPs for Dedicated and Private.
[01:32] Samira Khan: when you say gateway — is that a managed gateway or something we run? we have strict egress rules so would prefer a proxy in our VPC if possible.
[01:40] Luis: you can do either. hosted customers typically use our managed gateway which handles rate-limiting and routing; for Dedicated/Private we support a customer-run proxy or a VPC peering with our regional endpoints. some customers run an nginx sidecar or simple forwarder that additionally handles auth via SAML tokens. the SDK supports token refresh flows.
[01:58] Ethan Lee: how do we wire LangChain into our backend? we use LangChain for orchestration and LlamaIndex for vector stores. do you have example connectors?
[02:06] Luis: yes — we have LangChain Agents, Chains, and an embeddings wrapper in our SDK. note: some folks call it 'Lang Chain' in notes ;). we also include a LlamaIndex document loader example that uses our embeddings endpoint. there's a small diff between calling embeddings directly vs via LlamaIndex but it's pretty straightforward — i'll share the snippet after the call.
[02:25] Ben: any gotchas on tokenization or prompt size for embeddings? we've had issues where the tokenizer mismatch caused weird billing.
[02:32] Luis: good point. our docs list model tokenizer details; for embeddings we expose token counts in the response and the SDK can estimate costs locally. small mismatch sometimes happens if you preprocess with a different tokenizer, so we recommend using our tokenizer tools or the SDK helpers to consistent token counting.
[02:50] Priya: on quotas — we need burst handling. peak is...roughly 50k qpm during promos for text-gen with short prompts, steady-state maybe 5k qpm. can Dedicated support this with autoscaling?
[03:03] Avery: yes Dedicated is designed for predictable throughput and can be configured with reserved capacity + burst pools. Luis can give more on autoscale policies — we also provide policy-based routing so you can fallback to cheaper model variants during overload.
[03:15] Luis: on autoscale, you can set min/max GPU counts, and we support warm pools. for bursts we recommend a small dedicated baseline plus a burst capacity setting. also worth mentioning our smart routing — you can route by latency SLO, cost, or region, and fallback to a quantized variant if the primary is saturated.
[03:34] Samira: latency SLOs — do you provide per-route dashboards? we need tracing for each customer tenant.
[03:40] Luis: yes, in Redwood Console you get per-route/model dashboards, tracing hooks, and token-level cost breakdown. for Private deployments those metrics can be forwarded to your observability stack or exported via prometheus endpoints and we provide tracing spans compatible with open telemetry.
[03:56] Priya: security questions — SOC2, audit logs, SSO, and KMS. also data residency for EU customers.
[04:04] Avery: we are SOC2 certified, have RBAC and SSO/SAML support, audit logs, and KMS integrations (AWS KMS + customer managed keys for Private). for EU residency we have regional endpoints; Dedicated & Private give you stronger guarantees on data flow. i'll attach the security pack.
[04:20] Ethan: what about running LLMs on-prem? some of our big customers request an air-gapped deploy.
[04:26] Luis: Private supports on-prem packages; it's a heavier lift but possible. there are tradeoffs around model updates and telemetry — in air-gapped setups we do a manual bundle process and you manage model artifacts. we can provide a hardened inference runtime.
[04:39] Ben: instrumentation — we use DataDog and Honeycomb; can we get spans or logs for each request?
[04:45] Luis: yes, we integrate with OTLP for traces and push metrics to prometheus export. you can configure exporters to DataDog or Honeycomb. cost attribution per token is available too, and you can break it down by route or customer id.
[04:58] Priya: about rate-limits — is there a hard per-token throttle on hosted? how do you handle retries?
[05:05] Avery: hosted has default rate limits and quota tiers; near limits requests receive 429 with Retry-After. Dedicated allows custom quotas per account and you can set per-route limits. we also offer adaptive rate limiting to smooth bursts. for mission-critical paths customers often put a local queue/proxy in front to do retry backoff.
[05:22] Samira: would using a proxy increase latency much? we can't exceed our 250ms budget.
[05:27] Luis: a lightweight proxy (nginx or envoy) with keepalives adds a few ms. biggest factors are network RTT and model runtime. for sub-200ms gen you want a nearby regional Dedicated pool + short sequence lengths.
[05:41] Ben: curious — do you have benchmarks for common open models (like 7B quantized) with p50/p95 numbers?
[05:48] Luis: yes we publish model performance profiles in the catalog; i'll include a table with p50/p95 for 7B/13B variants and quantized configs. remember results depend on prompt length and batch size.
[06:00] Priya: what's the dev experience like — SDKs + local testing? we like to run unit tests that mock embeddings + generation.
[06:07] Luis: SDKs include local mocks and a playback mode for deterministic testing. we also have a CLI for quick calls and a dockerized envoy example. for LangChain/LlamaIndex tests you can mock the embeddings endpoint and inject deterministic vectors.
[06:21] Ethan: license and pricing — we need a ballpark for Dedicated (monthly commit) vs hosted per-token.
[06:27] Avery: i'll send a pricing matrix after this call; typical structure is usage-based for hosted and reserved monthly for Dedicated with discounts for commits. i'll include examples for Nova's estimated qpm.
[06:37] Priya: integration timeline — we want to run a 6-week POC, with a sandbox dataset and perf targets. whats next?
[06:45] Avery: propose: week 0 onboarding + credentials, week 1 integration (LangChain examples) + small demo, week 2 run benchmarks, weeks 3-5 tune Dedicated config, week 6 pilot with canary rollout. Luis, can you support a SE-led demo?
[06:56] Luis: yes, we'll prep a LangChain + LlamaIndex demo using your sample dataset, and run a quick benchmark showing p50/p95 and token cost.
[07:05] Ben: sample dataset — we'll share a sanitized subset of catalogs and edge-case queries.
[07:10] Samira: and i'll provide network/VPC requirements and firewall rules.
[07:14] Avery: great. recap of next steps: share SDK quickstart + LangChain snippets, share security docs, schedule SE demo, and pricing estimate.
[07:24] Priya: perfect. any other questions?
[07:27] Ethan: none from me. thanks.
[07:29] Avery: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with notes and the attachments.

End of transcript.
